answer: Age-graded action fee curve. Each identity’s first 100 actions cost 5× base; the multiplier decays 2% per verified active day to 1×, counting only non-transferable usage. An attacker launching 1,000 sybils pays 5,000× base across those first actions and waits weeks before normal rates; copied histories earn no credit. A sampled sonnet-length audit log checks usage. The schedule must mirror real non-transferable activity. Old identities may sit on a knoll of low fees, but that discount does not transfer.
